citation: Mantziou A., Hotte K., Cucuringu M., Reinert G. (2024) GDP nowcasting with large-scale inter-industry payment data in real time: a network approach. arXiv:2411.02029

dedupe_keys.name: gnar ex network autoregressive model for gdp nowcasting from inter industry payment data

description: GNAR-ex is an extended generalised network autoregressive model for networks whose edges carry time-varying weights and whose nodes carry time series, and it is used here to nowcast GDP for the whole economy and for individual industries from monthly payments between industries in the United Kingdom. It exploits neighbouring nodes and neighbouring edges in the payment network, was tested on synthetic data, and was optimised over nine quarterly GDP releases from the Office for National Statistics to be robust to revisions, beating autoregressive benchmarks. It was developed by Anastasia Mantziou, Kerstin Hotte, Mihai Cucuringu and Gesine Reinert and posted on arXiv on 4 November 2024. The preprint is available free online as a PDF; the abstract page gives no code link, and the payment data are not described as public. Caveats: it is a preprint, and results depend on access to granular payment data that few researchers hold. For simulation it shows how payment networks between industries can track economic activity in near real time, which could measure how an infrastructure outage or disaster spreads through supply and payment chains. It is related to the ECB investment fund contagion model record in this catalogue, another network model of financial flows.
